cover.hook: OpenAI explained exactly how ads now work inside ChatGPT conversations this week, the same week Canada landed one of the largest AI data centre leases in its history
cover.sub: Also this week: Canadian chipmaker Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion to challenge Nvidia, a major Canadian HR platform agreed to buy an AI company that interviews job candidates on its own, and Canva launched its first in-house AI image model, free to every user.

items.title: OpenAI explained this week exactly how ads now work inside ChatGPT conversations, built to stay separate from the answer itself
items.body: OpenAI published a detailed look at the ad stack now live inside ChatGPT, designed to read conversational intent and keep paid placements out of the answer itself, showing an ad only where the system judges it relevant. The company has said ChatGPT Ads has expanded to 26 new countries, with more than 100,000 advertisers now using the platform.
items.tease: Next: the same week Canada landed one of the largest AI infrastructure deals in its history.
items.reelLine: OpenAI explained how ads now work inside ChatGPT conversations this week.

items.title: Anthropic signed its first Canadian data centre lease this week, for the opening phase of a Nova Scotia project valued at more than $10 billion
items.body: EverWind Fuels' Point Tupper campus in Nova Scotia is valued at more than CA$10 billion in total: over $8 billion for the data centre campus and about $2 billion for an onshore wind portfolio built to help power it. Anthropic has signed a long term lease for the first 95 megawatt phase, targeted for late 2027, with a further 325 megawatt expansion proposed for 2028.
items.tease: Next: a Canadian-founded chip company raised its own record round this week.
items.reelLine: Anthropic signed its first Canadian data centre lease, in Nova Scotia, this week.

items.title: Canadian-founded chipmaker Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion this week, betting investors will back an open alternative to Nvidia's grip on AI chips
items.body: Tenstorrent closed a $1.5 billion US Series E at a $6.2 billion valuation, led by Trace Capital and Innovation X, with Fidelity, ARK Invest and Morgan Stanley also investing. The company builds open source RISC V processors for AI inference and says the funding will scale manufacturing of its Galaxy servers. Tenstorrent chose fresh funding over an earlier takeover approach from Intel and Qualcomm.
items.tease: Next: a Canadian HR platform's new deal, aimed at your own hiring.
items.reelLine: Canadian chipmaker Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion to challenge Nvidia this week.

items.title: Toronto based Dayforce agreed this week to buy an AI company that conducts job interviews on its own, day or night
items.body: Dayforce, the Canadian HR software platform used across the country for payroll and workforce management, signed a deal to acquire Ribbon AI, whose voice and video AI has already conducted more than a million job interviews for its clients. Dayforce plans to fold the technology into a new agentic recruiting feature; deal terms were not disclosed and the acquisition has not yet closed.
items.tease: Next: a free design tool that just got an AI model of its own.
items.reelLine: Dayforce agreed to buy an AI job interviewer company, Ribbon AI, this week.

items.title: Canva launched its first in-house AI image model this week, one that plans a design before it draws it
items.body: Canva Craft works in two steps: first it plans the layout, object placement and text, then it renders an image up to 2K resolution across roughly 30 aspect ratios. It is trained on Canva's own library of designed templates rather than photographs, and it is already available free to every Canva user through Dream Lab.
items.reelLine: Canva launched Craft, an AI image model that plans before it draws, this week.

summary.title: This week: Canada landed record AI money and infrastructure, while the tools a small business touches directly, ads, hiring and design, all got a jump

cover.hook: A Northwestern Ontario business can plan an ad visual with a free AI tool before ever booking a photographer
cover.sub: Canva launched its first in-house AI image model, Craft, this week, free to every Canva user. Here is the plain version of using it to mock up a real ad in about ten minutes.

list.title: Open Canva and look for Dream Lab
list.body: Canva Craft runs inside Canva's existing Dream Lab tool, free on every account, no new app or subscription needed.

list.title: Describe the ad in plain language, not a design brief
list.body: Craft's first step plans the layout, object placement and text before it draws anything, so a plain description of the product, setting and mood is enough to start.

list.title: Check the plan step before generating the image
list.body: Craft shows its layout plan first. Catching a wrong idea at that stage saves a redo later, something no stock photo subscription offers.

list.title: Generate at the resolution the ad actually needs
list.body: Craft renders up to 2K resolution across roughly 30 aspect ratios, enough for a Facebook post, an Instagram story and a print flyer from the same prompt.

list.title: Treat the first result as a draft, not the final ad
list.body: Craft is Canva's first version of this model. Review wording and any text it generates carefully before it goes out under your business's name.

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: A Northwestern Ontario retailer or tourism operator who could never afford a photographer for every seasonal promotion now has a free way to mock up a real visual first, and decide if it is worth the real photo shoot after.

cover.hook: Thunder Bay's public health unit now certifies food handlers anywhere in Canada through a fully online exam, not just at its own office
cover.sub: The Thunder Bay District Health Unit moved its food safety certification exam online, built on remote proctoring technology its vendor describes as AI-enabled, after years of running the test only in person.

posts.detailChip: Food Safety Certification, Thunder Bay District Health Unit
posts.title: What changed
posts.body: The Thunder Bay District Health Unit (TBDHU) requires every food premises to have at least one certified food handler on site under Ontario's food safety regulation, and for years that meant sitting the exam in person at the health unit's own office. TBDHU now runs that exam online through its "In Good Hands" course, requiring only a computer with a webcam and microphone rather than a trip to a health unit office. Talview, the company behind the remote proctoring platform, lists TBDHU as a customer on its own case study page, describing the system as AI-enabled remote proctoring that lets applicants test from anywhere in Canada. A passing score of 70% earns the Safe Food Handler certificate.

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: A restaurant, food truck or care home in a smaller Northwestern Ontario community no longer needs a staff member to travel into Thunder Bay, or wait for an in-person exam date, just to get a legally required certification. That is the unglamorous, practical version of AI adoption: not a new product, just one less trip and one less scheduling headache for a business that already has enough of both.

cover.hook: An AI interviewer that never sleeps is coming to the hiring software many Northwestern Ontario employers already use for payroll
cover.sub: Dayforce, the Canadian HR platform behind payroll and scheduling at organizations across the country, agreed this week to buy Ribbon AI, whose voice AI has already conducted more than a million job interviews. For health care and trades employers running a constant shortage, that changes who does the first round of hiring.

posts.detailChip: AI interview screening, what it means for health care and trades hiring
posts.title: What changed and what it means for Northwestern Ontario health care and trades employers
posts.body: Dayforce agreed this week to acquire Ribbon AI, a company whose voice and video AI conducts two way job interviews around the clock and hands recruiters a transcript and a scored summary; deal terms were not disclosed and the acquisition has not yet closed. Dayforce plans to build the technology into a new agentic recruiting feature inside its existing HR platform, used across Canada for payroll, scheduling and workforce management. For a Northwestern Ontario hospital, long term care home or trades employer that already runs a constant hiring shortage, with a small HR team fielding every application personally, an AI interviewer that can screen candidates overnight changes who gets a first look and how fast.

why.title: Why it matters here
why.body: Health care and trades are two of the sectors Northwestern Ontario's labour shortage hits hardest, and both already run lean HR teams that cannot interview every applicant quickly. An AI tool that does a first round screen does not replace the hiring decision, but it does remove the bottleneck that currently decides which applicants even get a human conversation.

cover.hook: A Northern Ontario program will cover half the cost of building and testing a new AI product, up to $2 million
cover.sub: NOHFC's Invest North Innovation stream funds applied research, demonstration and commercialization of new technology in Northern Ontario, AI products included, as a conditional contribution. Confirm your project's eligibility and funding cap with NOHFC before applying.

posts.title: Who it's for and how it works
posts.body: The Northern Ontario Heritage Fund Corporation's Invest North Innovation stream funds applied research, development, demonstration and commercialization of new technologies for private sector businesses in Northern Ontario, alone or partnered with an academic or research institution. Pure R&D projects can receive a conditional contribution covering up to 50% of eligible costs, capped at $500,000; projects that combine R&D with demonstration and commercialization, or cover demonstration and commercialization alone, can receive up to 50% of eligible costs, capped at $2 million. Combined federal and provincial government funding cannot exceed 75% of total eligible project costs, and intake is continuous. Eligible costs include technical labour, prototyping, testing and certification, and IP protection; land, working capital, and wages for an owner holding 10% or more of the business are not eligible.

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: Most Northern Ontario funding conversations assume AI help only means buying a tool off the shelf. Invest North Innovation is built for the other case: a Northwestern Ontario business actually developing or testing a new AI product, not just adopting one someone else built. Confirm your project's eligibility and the current funding cap directly with NOHFC before applying.

cover.hook: Northwestern Ontario businesses just got a third place customers can find them, inside a ChatGPT answer, and most have no idea it exists yet
cover.sub: OpenAI explained this week exactly how ads now work inside ChatGPT's conversations. The real shift isn't the ad format, it's that discovery is splitting into a channel most local marketing budgets aren't built for yet.

posts.title: Ads just moved inside the AI answer. Most Northwestern Ontario marketing budgets haven't noticed yet
posts.body: OpenAI published a detailed look this week at how ChatGPT's ad stack reads conversational intent and keeps paid placements separate from the answer itself, with ChatGPT Ads now live in 26 more countries and over 100,000 advertisers already using it. For a decade, a Northwestern Ontario business's entire online discovery strategy has meant one thing: rank on Google. That is no longer the whole picture. A growing share of the research a customer does, where to eat, who does renovations, which clinic to call, now happens inside an AI conversation instead of a search results page, and that conversation can now carry an ad the same way a search page does.

why.title: Why it matters here
why.body: A business that has spent years learning how to show up in a Google search result has spent zero years learning how to show up inside an AI conversation, because the channel did not exist until recently. The businesses that figure out early what makes an AI assistant mention them, not just rank them, are going to have a head start that is hard to close later. That is worth more attention locally than the ad format itself.
